title: Red Flags — When NOT to Treat (and What to Do Instead)

hook.en: Most back and neck pain is harmless. Learn to spot the few cases that aren't — and refer at the right speed.
hook.ur: Zyada tar back aur neck pain khatarnak nahi hota. Un chand cases ko pehchanna seekhein jo khatarnak hain — aur sahi raftaar se refer karein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll recognise the warning signs of serious pathology, know which need emergency vs urgent referral, and tell red flags from yellow flags.
goal.ur: End tak aap serious pathology ki warning signs pehchan sakenge, jaan jayenge ke kaun si emergency aur kaun si urgent referral mangti hai, aur red flags ko yellow flags se alag kar sakenge.

text.en: Here's the truth: most back and neck pain is not dangerous. But a small number of patients have something serious hiding behind ordinary-looking pain — a fracture, cancer, infection, cauda equina syndrome or a vascular problem. Your job isn't to diagnose these. It's to **notice the pattern and refer at the right speed**.
text.ur: Sach yeh hai: zyada tar back aur neck pain khatarnak nahi. Lekin chand patients mein aam se dard ke peeche koi serious cheez chhupi hoti hai — fracture, cancer, infection, cauda equina syndrome ya vascular masla. Aap ka kaam in ki diagnosis nahi. Aap ka kaam hai **pattern pehchanna aur sahi raftaar se refer karna**.

text.en: Think of yourself as a smoke detector, not the fire brigade. You don't put out the fire — you notice the smoke early and call the right people quickly. A detector that ignores smoke is dangerous; one that screams at every slice of toast is useless. Good screening sits in between.
text.ur: Khud ko fire brigade nahi, smoke detector samjhein. Aap aag nahi bujhate — aap dhuwan jaldi pehchan kar sahi logon ko foran bulate hain. Jo detector dhuwen ko nazar-andaz kare woh khatarnak hai; jo har toast par cheekhe woh bekaar. Achi screening in dono ke beech hai.

text.en:
Two kinds of flags:
**Red flags** — signs that may point to serious pathology → refer.
**Yellow flags** — psychological and social factors (fear, low mood, unhelpful beliefs, work stress) that can slow recovery → address them in YOUR care.
text.ur:
Do qism ke flags:
**Red flags** — nishaniyan jo serious pathology ki taraf ishara kar sakti hain → refer karein.
**Yellow flags** — nafsiyati aur samaji factors (dar, udaasi, ghalat khayalaat, kaam ka stress) jo recovery ko dheema kar sakte hain → in ko APNI care mein address karein.

simpler.en: Red flag = possible serious disease → refer. Yellow flag = mind/life factors → help in therapy.
simpler.ur: Red flag = mumkina serious beemari → refer. Yellow flag = zehan/zindagi ke factors → therapy mein madad.

title.en: The big five — clues and the right speed of action
title.ur: Bare paanch — ishare aur action ki sahi raftaar

rows.en: Saddle numbness, new bladder/bowel dysfunction, symptoms in both legs, sexual dysfunction
rows.ur: Saddle numbness, bladder/bowel ki nayi kharabi, dono legs mein symptoms, sexual dysfunction

rows.en: Significant trauma; or minor trauma with osteoporosis, long-term steroids or older age
rows.ur: Shadeed chot; ya osteoporosis, lambe arse ke steroids ya barhapay mein halki chot

rows.en: Past history of cancer (strongest clue), unexplained weight loss, constant pain not eased by rest or position
rows.ur: Cancer ki purani history (sab se mazboot ishara), be-wajah weight kam hona, musalsal dard jo aaram ya position se kam na ho

rows.en: Fever, recent infection, IV drug use, immunosuppression, recent spinal procedure
rows.ur: Bukhar, haal hi mein infection, IV drug use, weak immunity, haal hi mein spine ka procedure

rows.en: Pulsating abdominal pain/mass (aneurysm); neck: the 5 Ds & 3 Ns
rows.ur: Abdomen mein pulsating dard/swelling (aneurysm); neck: 5 Ds aur 3 Ns

rows.en: Emergency if acute or severe; no manual therapy
rows.ur: Achanak ya shadeed ho to emergency; manual therapy nahi

text.en: Neck vascular warning signs — **5 Ds and 3 Ns**: Dizziness, Diplopia (double vision), Dysarthria (slurred speech), Dysphagia (difficulty swallowing), Drop attacks · Nystagmus, Nausea, Numbness.
text.ur: Neck ke vascular warning signs — **5 Ds aur 3 Ns**: Dizziness (chakkar), Diplopia (do do nazar aana), Dysarthria (zaban larkharana), Dysphagia (nigalne mein mushkil), Drop attacks (achanak gir jana) · Nystagmus (aankhon ka larazna), Nausea (matli), Numbness (numbness).

question.en: A 45-year-old with low back pain reports numbness "where you sit on a bike seat" and difficulty starting to pass urine since yesterday. What do you do?
question.ur: 45 saal ke low back pain wale patient ko "jahan cycle ki seat lagti hai" wahan numbness hai aur kal se urine pass karne mein mushkil. Aap kya karenge?

text.en: Gentle mobilization today, review in a week
text.ur: Aaj naram mobilization, ek hafte baad review

feedback.en: This could be cauda equina syndrome — a week's delay can mean permanent loss of bladder or bowel function.
feedback.ur: Yeh cauda equina syndrome ho sakta hai — ek hafte ki dair bladder ya bowel function ka mustaqil nuqsan ban sakti hai.

text.en: Same-day emergency referral for suspected cauda equina syndrome
text.ur: Cauda equina syndrome ke shak par usi din emergency referral

feedback.en: Exactly. Saddle numbness + new bladder change = emergency. Explain why, help them get there today, and document it.
feedback.ur: Bilkul. Saddle numbness + bladder mein nayi tabdeeli = emergency. Wajah samjhayein, aaj hi pohanchne mein madad karein, aur document karein.

text.en: Home exercises and rest
text.ur: Ghar ki exercises aur aaram

feedback.en: Exercises can't treat nerve compression in the cauda equina. This needs emergency medical assessment.
feedback.ur: Exercises cauda equina mein nerve ke dabao ka ilaaj nahi kar saktin. Is ke liye emergency medical assessment chahiye.

text.en: Common mistakes: (1) Treating one flag in isolation — night pain alone, for example, is common in harmless back pain. Look for **clusters** and the whole story. (2) Screening once and never again — re-screen when symptoms change. (3) Vague questions like "any bladder problems?" — ask specifically: "Any change in feeling when you wipe after the toilet? Any difficulty starting or controlling your urine?"
text.ur: Aam ghaltiyan: (1) Ek flag ko akela dekhna — maslan sirf raat ka dard be-zarar back pain mein bhi aam hai. **Clusters** aur poori kahani dekhein. (2) Ek baar screen kar ke dobara na karna — symptoms badlein to dobara screen karein. (3) Mubham sawal jaise "bladder ka koi masla?" — khaas poochein: "Toilet ke baad saaf karte waqt feeling mein koi farq? Urine shuru karne ya rokne mein koi mushkil?"

prompt.en: Red flag or yellow flag? Sort each one.
prompt.ur: Red flag ya yellow flag? Har ek ko sort karein.

text.en: Unexplained weight loss
text.ur: Be-wajah weight kam hona

why.en: Can point to malignancy or systemic disease.
why.ur: Cancer ya systemic beemari ki taraf ishara ho sakta hai.

text.en: Believes "hurt means harm" and avoids all bending
text.ur: Yaqeen ke "dard = nuqsan" aur har jhukne se parhez

why.en: Fear-avoidance belief — address it with education and graded activity.
why.ur: Fear-avoidance belief — education aur graded activity se address karein.

text.en: Fever with constant back pain
text.ur: Bukhar ke saath musalsal back pain

text.en: Feels hopeless about ever getting better
text.ur: Theek hone ke baare mein na-ummeed

why.en: Low mood can slow recovery — support it, refer for psychology if severe.
why.ur: Udaasi recovery dheemi kar sakti hai — support karein, shadeed ho to psychology ke liye refer.

text.en: Past history of cancer
text.ur: Cancer ki purani history

why.en: The strongest single clue for spinal malignancy.
why.ur: Spinal malignancy ka sab se mazboot akela ishara.

text.en: Worried about losing their job; off work for weeks
text.ur: Naukri jaane ka dar; hafton se kaam se chutti

why.en: Work and social stress — a classic yellow (sometimes called blue/black) flag.
why.ur: Kaam aur samaji stress — classic yellow (kabhi blue/black bhi kehte hain) flag.

text.en: Saddle anaesthesia
text.ur: Saddle anaesthesia

why.ur: Cauda equina ka warning sign — emergency.

text.en: What to do with yellow flags: don't send them away — they're part of **your** job. Validate, explain pain simply, set graded goals together and gently challenge unhelpful beliefs (see the Pain Science lesson). Severe or persistent distress may need psychology input alongside physiotherapy.
text.ur: Yellow flags ke saath kya karein: unhein bahar na bhejein — yeh **aap** ke kaam ka hissa hain. Tasleem karein, dard ko asaani se samjhayein, mil kar graded goals banayein aur ghalat khayalaat ko narmi se challenge karein (Pain Science lesson dekhein). Shadeed ya musalsal pareshani mein physiotherapy ke saath psychology ki madad chahiye ho sakti hai.

text.en: Before any manual therapy to the neck: screen for vascular pathology and upper cervical instability, and **stop immediately** if dizziness, visual disturbance, speech change or any new neurological symptom appears. Document what you screened and what you found.
text.ur: Neck par kisi bhi manual therapy se pehle: vascular pathology aur upper cervical instability ke liye screen karein, aur agar chakkar, nazar mein tabdeeli, bolne mein farq ya koi naya neurological symptom aaye to **foran ruk jayein**. Jo screen kiya aur jo mila, document karein.

question.en: Which of these is a YELLOW flag?
question.ur: In mein se YELLOW flag kaun sa hai?

text.en: Constant night pain not changed by any position
text.ur: Raat ka musalsal dard jo kisi position se na badle

feedback.en: That's a possible red flag (needs the whole picture) — not a psychosocial factor.
feedback.ur: Yeh mumkina red flag hai (poori tasveer chahiye) — psychosocial factor nahi.

text.en: A strong belief that the back is "damaged" and must be rested
text.ur: Pakka yaqeen ke back "kharab" hai aur aaram zaroori hai

feedback.en: Yes — an unhelpful belief that drives fear and avoidance. You can change this with education and graded activity.
feedback.ur: Haan — ek nuqsan-deh khayal jo dar aur parhez barhata hai. Education aur graded activity se ise badla ja sakta hai.

text.en: Unexplained weight loss of 6 kg
text.ur: 6 kg be-wajah weight kam hona

feedback.en: That's a red flag — it needs medical assessment.
feedback.ur: Yeh red flag hai — medical assessment chahiye.

question.en: During neck mobilization, the patient suddenly feels dizzy and sees double. What now?
question.ur: Neck ki mobilization ke dauraan patient ko achanak chakkar aata hai aur do do nazar aata hai. Ab kya?

text.en: Continue more gently
text.ur: Aur naram tareeqe se jaari rakhein

feedback.en: No — dizziness + diplopia are vascular warning signs. Never continue.
feedback.ur: Nahi — chakkar + diplopia vascular warning signs hain. Kabhi jaari na rakhein.

text.en: Stop immediately, keep them safe and arrange urgent medical assessment
text.ur: Foran ruk jayein, patient ko mehfooz rakhein aur urgent medical assessment ka intezam karein

feedback.en: Correct. Stop, monitor, don't let them leave alone, arrange urgent assessment and document everything.
feedback.ur: Sahi. Ruk jayein, monitor karein, akela jaane na dein, urgent assessment ka intezam karein aur sab document karein.

text.en: Switch to the other side of the neck
text.ur: Neck ki doosri taraf shift ho jayein

feedback.en: The symptom is the warning, not the side. Stop all neck techniques.
feedback.ur: Warning symptom hai, side nahi. Neck ki har technique rok dein.

text.en: Honest evidence: most single red flags have poor diagnostic accuracy on their own — many people with a flag don't have serious disease, and some with serious disease have few flags. That's why international frameworks stress **clinical reasoning**: the combination of flags, the patient's story and how symptoms behave over time.
text.ur: Imaandar evidence: zyada tar akele red flags ki diagnostic accuracy weak hai — bohat se logon mein flag hota hai magar serious beemari nahi, aur kuch serious beemari walon mein flags kam hote hain. Isi liye international frameworks **clinical reasoning** par zor dete hain: flags ka combination, patient ki kahani aur waqt ke saath symptoms ka rawaiya.

text.en: One line: **Notice the pattern, refer at the right speed, document what you asked.**
text.ur: Ek line: **Pattern pehchanein, sahi raftaar se refer karein, jo poocha woh document karein.**

summary.en: Red flags suggest serious pathology → refer; yellow flags are psychosocial → address in your care.
summary.ur: Red flags serious pathology ki taraf → refer; yellow flags psychosocial → apni care mein address.

summary.en: Saddle numbness or new bladder/bowel change = same-day emergency (cauda equina).
summary.ur: Saddle numbness ya bladder/bowel mein nayi tabdeeli = usi din emergency (cauda equina).

summary.en: Look for clusters, re-screen when things change, and stop neck techniques at any 5D/3N sign.
summary.ur: Clusters dekhein, halaat badlein to dobara screen karein, aur kisi bhi 5D/3N sign par neck ki techniques rok dein.

front.ur: Cauda equina syndrome ke warning signs?

back.en: Saddle numbness, new bladder/bowel dysfunction, bilateral leg symptoms, sexual dysfunction → same-day emergency.
back.ur: Saddle numbness, bladder/bowel ki nayi kharabi, dono legs mein symptoms, sexual dysfunction → usi din emergency.

back.en: Dizziness, Diplopia, Dysarthria, Dysphagia, Drop attacks · Nystagmus, Nausea, Numbness.
back.ur: Dizziness, Diplopia, Dysarthria, Dysphagia, Drop attacks · Nystagmus, Nausea, Numbness.

front.en: Strongest single clue for spinal malignancy?
front.ur: Spinal malignancy ka sab se mazboot akela ishara?

back.en: Red = possible serious pathology (refer). Yellow = psychosocial barriers to recovery (address in care).
back.ur: Red = mumkina serious pathology (refer). Yellow = recovery ki psychosocial rukawatein (care mein address).

front.en: Why look for clusters of red flags?
front.ur: Red flags ke clusters kyun dekhein?

back.en: Single flags have poor accuracy on their own; combinations plus the story are more informative.
back.ur: Akele flags ki accuracy weak hai; combinations aur kahani zyada maloomat dete hain.

note.ur: Dekhein PNA safety warnings kaise screen karta hai.

note.ur: Yellow flags ko ache se kaise handle karein.
